title: P6 ScheduleOptions Release 26 Field Disposition
reference_version: Oracle Primavera P6 EPPM REST API Release 26
rule: Every current Release 26 ScheduleOptions REST field must have an explicit disposition. Metadata fields are classified separately from calculation-core options. Historical Integration API-only extensions are not silently treated as current REST fields. A typed internal representation does not certify lossless interchange-to-domain mapping; PriorityList and ResourceList remain pending until explicit adapter and authoritative resource-leveling regression evidence exist.

open_mapping_gaps.reason: The Release 26 REST schema exposes PriorityList as a scalar string, while the Integration API contract exposes String[]. The REST encoding into ordered PriorityListItem entries, including sort-order representation/defaults, is not established by the cited REST schema; a source-backed adapter and round-trip/resource-leveling evidence remain outstanding.

The canonical Shared Core domain and snapshot path preserve ResourceList as an ordered tuple/JSON array, including resource IDs containing commas. The remaining gap is the external wire adapter: Release 26 REST exposes a scalar string while the Integration API exposes String[], and the cited REST schema does not establish a lossless encoding/escaping rule. Keep this field pending until a source-backed REST adapter and round-trip/resource-leveling evidence exist.

known_gaps.detail: Twelve of the 13 documented P6 priority criteria now have distinct internal value/comparator paths through the typed boundary and leveling core: Activity ID, Activity Leveling Priority, Early Start, Early Finish, Late Start, Late Finish, Free Float, Planned Finish, Project Planned Start, Project Priority, Remaining Duration, and Total Float. The documented Activity Leveling Priority is a string enum (Top/High/Normal/Low/Lowest), not the separate internal numeric activity_priority field. It propagates through the scheduling Activity model and ActivityMaster storage; the documented default Normal is applied to new and legacy-null records. Planned Finish is distinct; explicit values are preserved, and a CPM fallback is permitted only for unstarted activities with no actual dates. Project Priority comes from the authoritative project-leveling-priority snapshot (1 highest through 100 lowest). Core and persistence support are not complete end-to-end certification: canonical XER/REST import materialization into ActivityMaster and onward into the schedule Activity is still not demonstrated losslessly. Original/Planned Duration remains blocked because its context-dependent source semantics and external adapter contract are not established; the ambiguous original_or_planned_duration alias remains rejected.
Current SortOrder enum supports ASCENDING and DESCENDING only; P6 hierarchy sort semantics are not represented.

Regression coverage includes Project Priority in both directions and the authoritative multi-project snapshot path; Activity Leveling Priority enum values, documented Normal default, ascending/descending selection, public scheduler propagation, and SQLite/PostgreSQL persistence; and Planned Finish ordering, fail-closed behavior after activity start, public scheduler sourcing, and storage/migration. Remaining acceptance must cover Original/Planned Duration resolution, stable ties and mixed-field precedence for every documented criterion, Hierarchy sort, canonical XER/REST → ActivityMaster → Shared Core import/materializer round-trip, lossless REST/interchange PriorityList/ResourceList encoding and escaping, Project Planned Start provenance, and deterministic backward retry acceptance.

priority_list_compatibility_audit.compatibility_rule: The current PR #1457 implements 12 of the 13 documented P6 priority criteria internally; Original/Planned Duration remains unresolved. The documented Activity Leveling Priority is the Top/High/Normal/Low/Lowest enum and defaults to Normal; the separate numeric activity_priority field is not a substitute. Planned Finish and Project Priority have distinct core and persistence paths, but canonical import/materializer provenance and lossless external PriorityList/ResourceList round-trip are not yet certified. Keep the feature PR Draft until the remaining source-backed gates and independent semantic review pass.
priority_list_compatibility_audit.source_version: P6 Professional User Guide Version 26; relevant online pages last published 2026-05-29

documented_rules.rule: Priority row order is precedence order: each row takes precedence over every row below it. Priority rows are used only when multiple activities compete for the same resource at the same time.

If multiple activities are ready for leveling, the leveler applies the configured priority rows. For Activity ID ordering, number-like values sort before alphabetic values and blanks; when no priority codes are configured, Activity ID is the default.

The documented priority table has 13 fields and supports ascending and descending; Hierarchy appears only for hierarchical fields. The internal model and leveling comparators now represent 12 criteria, including Activity Leveling Priority (Top/High/Normal/Low/Lowest), Planned Finish, and Project Priority. Original/Planned Duration remains blocked until the context-dependent source rule and adapter mapping are proven.

reviewed_paths.finding: The typed boundary accepts distinct activity_leveling_priority, planned_finish, and project_priority criteria alongside earlier criteria. Activity Leveling Priority uses its own enum; the separate numeric internal activity_priority is not treated as equivalent. The ambiguous original_or_planned_duration label remains rejected.
reviewed_paths.required_acceptance: Implement the source-backed Original/Planned Duration resolver; add public tests for state-dependent selection, all directions and stable ties; then verify canonical wire round-trip.

reviewed_paths.finding: The scheduler preserves explicit Planned Finish and only uses initial CPM Early Finish as a calculated fallback for unstarted activities with no actual dates. Started activities do not silently alias missing Planned Finish. Activity Leveling Priority is propagated from Activity.leveling_priority; the documented default is Normal. Project Priority is propagated from each authoritative project snapshot.
reviewed_paths.required_acceptance: Verify field values through authoritative REST/XER import and ActivityMaster-to-schedule materialization; add end-to-end round-trip evidence, progress-state checks and independent semantic review.

reviewed_paths.finding: Activity Leveling Priority is a distinct Top/High/Normal/Low/Lowest enum; Project Priority is a distinct 1–100 value where 1 is highest and 100 lowest. Since this comparator selects activities to move, it is inverse to allocation precedence, moving lower-precedence contributors first under contention. Missing values on direct leveling slices fail closed.
reviewed_paths.required_acceptance: Complete mixed-field precedence and tie acceptance for both directions and compare each documented criterion to versioned Release 26 definitions.

reviewed_paths.finding: ActivityMaster validates and round-trips Planned Finish and Activity Leveling Priority in SQLite and PostgreSQL. Existing schemas receive additive columns; legacy NULL Activity Leveling Priority values become the source-defined Normal default. Exact-head database integration and legacy-null migration tests are present.
reviewed_paths.required_acceptance: Connect and test the authoritative XER/REST import path to ActivityMaster and the canonical scheduling Activity without lossy aliases; preserve unknown/manual values and prove restart/reload/export round-trip.
